To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ethanolic extracts from the leaves of Lippia albe, Aegle marmorosa and L. nodifloral showed the maximum zone of inhibition against the clinical isolates of Pseudomonas, E.coli and Klebsiela, respectively.
the extracts of L. alba (Mill), L. nodifloral, A. marmelos and C. infortunatum showed significant antimicrobial activities against pathogenic E. coli, K. Pneumonia and P. aeruginosa.
the ethanolic extract of Lippia albo (Mill) Cler and L. nodiflorae L. showed maximum antimicrobial activity against the test organisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of antimicrobial activity of some common Indian medicinal plant extracts.
the study of the antimicrobial activities of the ethanolic and the methanolic extracts against pathogenic clinical isolates.
the antimicrobial activity of the ethanolic and the methanolic plant leaf extracts against the urinary tract infecting pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plant extracts of the four selected plants are effective against the test organisms and can be further used as a potential source of natural antibacterial agents.

ethanolic extract of L. nodoflora is the most effective against the pathogenic strains of E.coli and P. aeruginosa and methanolic extract of A.marmelos is the most effective among all the plants against K. pneumoniae.
the ethanolic and aqueous extracts of the plants are effective in inhibiting the growth of pathogenic E.coli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plant extracts of L. alba and L. nodifora have the potential to inhibit the growth of the test organisms and could be used as a potential antibacterial agent.
these plant extracts can be used as a potential alternative for antibiotics and also for green synthesized nanoparticles.
the ethanolic extracts were more effective against all the organisms tested in this study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these plants are rich in secondary metabolites and can be used for antimicrobial activity and as an alternative medicine.
the ethanolic extracts were more effective than the methanolic extract of all the plants tested.
these extracts could be used as a source of new antimicrobial compounds.
